item.title: Spring Break Reading Activities for Families
item.description:
Reading activities during Spring Break help maintain student literacy skills while making reading feel like play, not schoolwork. Suggested activities include: reading a book then watching its movie adaptation (like Charlotte's Web or Curious George), reading about places visited during travel (zoos, museums, natural areas), and doing family read-alouds where everyone takes turns reading and discussing the book over meals or campfires. Contact your student's Reading Corner teacher with questions.

item.title: March 2026 Breakfast and Lunch Menus
item.description:
Marshall Elementary has released its breakfast and lunch menus for March 2026.

Breakfast highlights include chocolate donuts, breakfast pizza, egg & cheese sandwiches, mini pancakes, glazed donuts, biscuits & gravy, French toast varieties, and themed items for St. Patrick's Day and spring. All breakfasts include 100% fruit juice, apples, oranges or other fresh fruit, and choice of milk.

Lunch highlights feature cheeseburgers, walking tacos, BBQ chicken, pizza options, chicken nuggets, spaghetti, hot dogs, chicken patties, mozzarella sticks, and special St. Patrick's Day and spring-themed meals. Choice of milk is included with every lunch.

Spring break begins March 30-31, 2026.

item.title: Book Fair Volunteer Requirements
item.description:
Marshall Elementary is hosting a Scholastic Book Fair March 9th-12th. Volunteers must have a completed volunteer application on file before helping. item.title: February Reading Corner: Understanding Decoding Skills
item.description:
Decoding is the foundational reading skill of recognizing letter sounds and patterns and blending them together to read words aloud. The process involves recognizing letters and letter patterns (like b, sh, igh), knowing their sounds, and blending those sounds to read words (e.g., /c/ - /a/ - /t/ becomes "cat"). Grade-specific decoding activities and resources are available from Reading Rockets for Kindergarten, First Grade, Second Grade, and Third Grade (video showing syllable strategies for longer words).

Marshall Elementary has released its breakfast and lunch menus for February 2026.
